notes.title: Nexus 5X v1.0 Release
notes.notes:
Nexus 5X v1.0 Release

Hello everyone.

Welcome to the Nexus 5X 1.0 launch! We are super excited to take Nexus 5X out of Early Access.

eXplore – eXpand – eXploit – eXterminate - EXPRESS
Nexus 5X takes the core pillars of the 4X genre - deep strategy, tense diplomatic drama, and epic military encounters - and distils them into a fast-paced competitive format that is perfect for short-run sessions, allowing groups of up to eight players to complete a full playthrough together in around an hour.

If you are new to the game, we at Whatboy Games, hope you will have as much fun discovering and playing the game as we have had making it! Please join our Discord community to discuss the game, arrange games or just to hang out!

To those who have been with us through Early Access, a heartfelt thank you from all of us! Much of the quality of the game is built on your feedback and continued support. We hope you enjoy all the changes outlined below and will continue to be awesome and welcome new members into the Nexus 5X community.

The Whatboy Team





Patch Notes v1.0

New Faction – The Keepers of Ave'brenn

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/cbd16def5555f421da8d193487f179d2a1b1a4f2.png

“From the moment that consciousness was achieved and the Khennet awoke, so did awaken the prophet Brehkk.”

The Keepers of Ave’brenn join the race for galactic dominance! A deeply spiritual, lithoid species comes to spread their message throughout the galaxy.

 The Keepers are a highly religious faction that accumulate Faith to spread their Culture automatically.
 They can ordain Archdruids on Cultured planets to double the culture resource gains from that system.
 However, their sedentary nature means it costs additional Support every time you move a fleet.


New and Update Feature

UI Scale
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/e5151ed3d58076022eb2b4445ec6beeadcb5ac64.png

 Added a UI Scale bar to the options menu to change the size of the UI on screen.


Ranked Matchmaking

 You can now matchmake with other players automatically for ranked games.



Balance Updates

General

 Spaceborne: To make things a little clearer, Spaceborne no longer have Combat Advantage over other fleets, but their Strength has been increased accordingly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/132f4c4630b6c1cea8368951527ac745551fb560.png

Technologies

 Graviton Explosives (Physics VII): Reduced Capital ship strength bonus to +1 (from +2) and removed ‘Core Mine’ project unlock. (Moved to Terraforming).
 Zero Point Reactor (Physics VII): Reduced ship strength bonus to +1 (from +2), added +1 Ranged Attack for Ranged fleets.
 Tachyon Lances (Physics VIII): Now gives +4 Strength to Capital ships instead of all ships.
 Giga Cannon (Physics VIII): Changed effect text to, ‘Ships in this fleet gain {Weapons}[Weapons/] and this fleet gains an additional {Firepower|%}[Weapons/] if Flanking an enemy.’ for clarity.



 Plasteel Materials (Nano-Tech IV): Now gives an additional +1 Ranged Attack to Ranged ships.

 Kinetic Artillery (Nano-Tech V): Increased Dreadnought base Strength to 11 (from 10).

Increased Council Votes bonus from ‘Kha’lanka Crystal Plant’ project to 8 (from 5). Increased ship Strength bonus from ‘Chemical Plant’ project to +2 (from +1).

notes.title: Early Access Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

We've got a big announcement going out tomorrow (21st) but wanted to give you all a heads up before the rest of the world.

We've learned a huge amount about the way that gamers play our game throughout the Early Access period so far, and we're pushing hard towards finalizing the game for its 1.0 launch.

Early Access is a great opportunity for developers to make changes to their games and to adjust any aspect of the experience that they think could be better.

As you all know, we've added new factions, leaders and game systems during Early Access, but from tomorrow one fairly big thing about the game will change - its name.

From tomorrow, the game will be renamed from 'Stellaris Nexus' to 'Nexus 5X'.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/dec61cdfbd64d9885896815b93e08a61216aa119.jpg

We're leveling up the 4X genre with an extra X, which stands for EXPRESS.

We feel that one of the most unique features of our game is that it offers all of the strategic depth of a 4X game, but in a short-run (about 60 mins) format - which is why we're adding EXPRESS to the 4X genre and renaming the game to reflect that.

We'll also be announcing the 1.0 launch date of Nexus 5X tomorrow during the Future Games Show, so keep an eye out for that!

Thanks for all of your help and support throughout Early Access - we couldn't have done it without you!

notes.title: Patch Notes v0.32
notes.notes:
Patch Notes v0.32

Hello everyone.

Hope everyone is doing well. This latest update introduces a number of updates to core systems to help balance out different approaches to winning the game along with dedicated servers and ranked play for our more competitive players!

We’ve also been looking at some balancing issues to keep tech and trait picks healthy.

As always, please let us know what you think!


New Features

Ranked and Dedicated Servers
This update introduces new ways to play the game in multi-player. You can now select from 1 of 3 different server modes when hosting a Custom lobby.


 Local Server: As before the lobby host will host the game locally on their PC. Allows any game settings, save-games and late-joining players.
 Dedicated Server: Host the game on an official dedicated server. Dedicated servers must feature a turn-timer.
 Ranked Server: Compete against other players in a ranked game.



Ranked Mode
Players can now compete against each other in official ranked games to improve their Ranked Elo and discover who is truly suited to rule the Galaxy!


 Ranked games will affect your personal Ranked Elo.
 Ranked games begin with a pre-game leader ban and draft phase to ensure a healthy leader spread.
 Ranked games feature default turn-timer and game length.
 You need at least 4 players and no AI to start the game.




Mechanics Updates

Diplomacy and Pacts
We’ve updated the way diplomacy and pacts work to encourage more careful consideration of pacts and deals with other empires and to balance out some very powerful non-aggression strategies.


 You are now limited to 2 pacts with each other Empire (modifiable by Traits and Tech).
 All mutually beneficial deals now grant a flat reward of 1 Succession.
 Breaking a pact always costs 2 Succession.



Espionage Overhaul
In this build we’ve flipped around how espionage works to help make it more impactful without making it too oppressive for the victims.


 The Espionage edict now places a Spy on a planet instead of a plot.
 Spies are discoverable and removable in the same way as plots and will tick up in strength every turn.
 You can immediately use a Spy to activate a plot on a planet if the Spy is of sufficient strength.
 Reworked some plots including the dreaded ‘Graviton Bomb’.
 Coups are no longer possible on Nexus as it became too much of an automatic choice.



Balance Updates

Advanced Fleets

 Improved the Strength and reduced the Munitions cost of unlockable fleet types to make the techs more desirable.


Advanced Megastructures

 Reduced the Succession reward for all faction Megastructures to 3.


Technologies
We’ve been focusing on some of the least picked techs to try to bring them up to scratch.


 Advanced Navigation Computer (Physics II): Changed effect to: ’ Your Raider Fleets gain +1 Speed and can move through nebulae without stopping.’
 Sentry Array (Physics VII): Changed effect to: ‘Grants Sensor Vision over the whole galaxy. You can Explore in any visible system, including hazardous systems.’
 Hyperdrive (Physics VIII): Changed effect to: ‘All of your fleets gain +2 Speed.’
 Mining Drones (Nano-Tech I): Moved to tech level 2.
 Mineral Probes (Nano-Tech II): Moved to tech level 1.
 Advanced Damage Control (Nano-Tech III): Changed effect to: ‘Gain +1 Munitions every time one of your ships is destroyed.’
 Nanite Bio Weapons (Nano-Tech VII): Added passive effect: ‘Your fleets can perform an additional activation after occupying a planet.’

Good to be back into it after Christmas, Covid and the New Year. I hope you are all having a fantastic 2024 so far!

As always, please let us know what you think!

notes.title: Patch Notes v0.28.5646
notes.notes:
Hello everyone.

Great to see so many people enjoying the game over the last few weeks! We’ve been busy fixing bugs, listening to everyone’s great feedback and looking at our internal data to put out our first Early Access update before we take a break for Christmas.

This update focuses on addressing a few balance issues around Culture and certain leaders, by updating Culture to make its play more tactical, rather than just trying to be the player to spam out the most Culture.

We’ve also got some more asynchronicity between the factions with Faction specific pacts as well as some more variety in Techs, Titles and Resolutions.

As always, please let us know what you think!

Gameplay Changes

Tactical Culture
Culture is something we’ve wanted to rework a bit for a while and given the dominance of culture focused leaders and strategies since the beta release, we wanted to start this process before disappearing for our end of year break.

The idea is to not nerf these strategies, but to give culture more gameplay utility, rather than just scoring large amounts of Succession.


 The Culture title now works differently. You can score a maximum of 5 Succession at each council, based on how much culture you have spread throughout the galaxy compared to other Empires.
 Cultures, base +1 Vote benefit has been replaced with a benefit based on the planet type.
 Advanced planets grant +2 Research, +2 Trade Value.
 Rich planets grant +2 Materials income.
 Industrial planets grant +5 Munitions.
 Populous planets grant +4 Council Votes.


Fleet Advantage

 Fleets now deal +50% damage against disadvantaged fleets as well as taking -50% damage.
 This is to ensure that the advantage still has a significant effect when fighting against a much larger fleet.



New Content

Faction Pacts

 To give some more options when forming pacts with your rivals, each Faction now comes with its own unique pact that can be offered or requested when dealing with that faction.
 Try to make the right friends!


Additional Content

 New Titles, Resolutions and Technologies to look out for!



Balance Changes

To start off, we are introducing some slight balance tweaks to leaders who are levelling up way quicker than the rest.

Leaders

 UNE Diplomat: Reduced XP gain from pacts to 20 (from 25).
 Voor Teacher: Reduced XP gain from trading techs to 6 per tech level (from 8).
 Voor Explorer: Reduced XP gain from exploration to 10 / 4 (from 15 / 5).
 Kel-Azaan Hunter: Reduced XP gain to 25 (from 30).


Ultimate Edicts

 Versatile (UNE): This Edict’s effect is now: ‘This turn, whenever you play an Edict, draw an Edict. (This Edict is not returned to your queue until the end of the turn.)’


Military Tech

 Reduced the base Strength bonus of all military tech by 1 across the board.
 This is to even out the tech picks with and across the tech branches.
 To make it a bit harder (but still possible) to build up your unstoppable death balls!



Matchmaking

 Removed AI players from matchmade games.


Important Bug Fixes

 Fixed all clients being disconnected at the end of a 150 turn game.
 Fixed clients being kicked off the summary screen if the host quits the game.
 Fixed being able to get duplicate techs through exploration.
 Numerous stability and typo fixes.

notes.title: Stellaris Nexus - aka "Stellaris in an hour" - delays its early access release for a week-long open beta
notes.notes:
Stellaris Nexus hinges off one of the downsides of the Paradox space game’s epic scale - the amount of time it takes to finish a match - to present a bite-sized side dish of 4X nibbles if you only have an hour to play instead of, say, a day. Now that plate of nibbles is offering up, er, a basically identical plate of bite-sized nibbles that you don’t have to pay for right away, as the game has seen its early access release date - planned for tomorrow, no less - replaced by a last-minute week-long open beta.

 Read more

notes.title: New Stellaris game finally has an early access release date
notes.notes:
The new Stellaris game, Stellaris Nexus, is a little different to what we've seen before. With Crusader Kings 3, Cities Skylines 2, and of course Stellaris itself, Paradox has mastered the grand-scale, sweeping strategy sim designed to last for hours. There's nothing like losing yourself in the meticulous tactics and intricate head canon of a long-running campaign, but let's be real - you don't always have the time. What if you want the thrill of Stellaris, but compacted into 60 minutes? How about a full round of multiplayer, but short enough you can squeeze it in before work? This is Stellaris Nexus, and it's finally got a confirmed early access release date.
Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Development Diary #3 & Release Date Announcement!
notes.notes:
Before we get to the Dev Diary, we want to take this opportunity to announce the Early Access release date for Stellaris Nexus! We're very happy to share that in just a week, on 5th December, you will be able to dive in and play the game for yourself! We've prepared a date announcement trailer for you right here:

[previewyoutube=nM3pUiikA4I;full][/previewyoutube]
Now back to our regularly scheduled Dev Diary...

Succession & New League Council
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/97548ac57271852a834a14aa66034e3d3d4b0049.png

Hi and welcome to another Stellaris Nexus Dev Diary. Today we're going be talking about the galactic council and succession and how players win the game through accumulating succession points.

[previewyoutube=KTerPLtlhRI;full][/previewyoutube]
Succession
Stellaris Nexus isn't an out and out war game. The objective of the game isn't to conquer the galaxy but prove that you're most suited to lead it.

In the aftermath of the collapse of the Tzynn empire, the galactic populous are looking for strong leader, someone who can lead the Galaxy to stability and prosperity. A leader who is proven.
So the objective of the game is to prove that YOU are the best choice to succeed the fallen Tzynn Emperor as the new emperor of the galaxy.

Players will do that by earing succession points throughout the game. And the aim of the game is to have 100 succession points coming out of a galactic council meeting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/25af0559a33fde28136c7157ac095dcd161ea374.png

What makes this idea of succession so compelling is that it can take a number of different forms. Succession gives you a lot of different routes to victory.

Depending on your play style, you can develop your economy to build giant mega structures or spread your culture to other factions or you can engage in diplomacy to promote stability throughout the galaxy. The more pacts that you make the more succession points you will gain or you can go for the all important titles that are voted in by all factions when the New League Council meets every eight years.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/16bceffeccb7cf60acfb02a3e3cab77d3bd5a1af.gif
The New League Council
At the meetings of the New League Council, the various achievements of the factions are recognized and succession points are awarded, but most importantly, players then vote on which new titles and resolutions are going to be adopted moving forward in the game. This gives players the choice and the power to decide who wins and how they win by putting the victory conditions for the game in the hands of the players.

Each council, players get a number of titles to vote on and whichever title get adopted will join the victory conditions for the rest of the game. In that way, we let players as a as a group, decide on how that game is going to go. If they vote in lots of economic titles, they’re probably going to have a fairly friendly game, but with a few sort of key skirmishes over key economic planets.

Whereas if you go for more military focused titles or territory focused titles, you're really going to see a lot more conflict and hostility.

But it's not just titles - there's also resolutions that can be voted on at each council phase.
Once a title is adopted, it's then there for the rest of the game, whereas resolutions only have an effect between council phases and then get completely revoked and replaced at the next council.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/5dd190fc9b115013413e5db8b1827bd4824fb7ec.gif
 
These dual systems (of Titles and Resolutions) is an important piece of design, because it ensures that players always have an interesting choice when it comes to voting during the council phase.

If there's a title that you really want to win, obviously, you're going to put a lot of your votes behind that. But if can see that the rest of the factions are likely to support that Title anyway, then those votes can feel like they’re wasted. So, instead you can choose to put those votes on a resolution which have an immediate impact and can change the game some massive way.
For example, the Unity resolution creates a non-aggression pact between all factions. So if you need to slow down the game a bit by removing aggression between factions, that's a great one to go for.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224818/d07b5213dc368817e2c34b3b02c34394303e257c.png

Stellaris Nexus is a fast 4X game designed to be played, start to finish in about 60 minutes, but every game plays out very differently, not only as a result of the factions that players choose, but also the decisions that they collectively make when the council meets. The titles and resolutions that receive the most votes have a huge impact on the path to victory for all players.

But there can only be one winner. And it's the player who manages to navigate that path most successfully that will ascend victorious to the throne on Nexus and take the crown as the new emperor of the galaxy.
